The test image shows a corn ear (pod/seed) with white/grayish-white fluffy mycelium growing on kernels in the middle portion of the ear. Top candidates from pod/seed classes: Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Fusarium_Disease, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Gibberella_Disease, Aspergillus_Ear_Rot.

Now viewing reference images one at a time:

I've used all 8 reference views. Here's my analysis:

**Test image**: Corn ear with white/grayish-white fluffy cottony mycelium concentrated in a band/region on kernels, surrounding kernels are yellow and healthy.

**Reference comparisons**:
- **Aspergillus**: olive-green powdery — clearly different
- **Gibberella**: pink/red mold at tip — different color
- **Trichoderma**: dark blue-green mold on husk — different
- **Diplodia pod (42)**: severely rotted brown ear — different stage/appearance
- **Diplodia seed (41)**: cross-section white mycelium — different view
- **Fusarium seed (25)**: white scattered mycelium on kernels with surrounding yellow kernels — most similar to test image
- **Fusarium seed (42)**: white mycelium band on ear — moderately similar

The test image most closely matches Fusarium_Disease: white to whitish-gray fluffy mycelium growing on a region of the ear with surrounding healthy yellow kernels. The mold doesn't show clear pink tint or starburst, but the overall appearance (white cottony growth on kernels in a concentrated area) best matches the Fusarium references.
